Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the time last week. We're starting to assemble the SIG/CAIQ intake for HelixBank and want to align on evidence phasing across ISO27001 and FedRAMP expectations. Two quick asks so we can map resources on our side: 

1) Do you have a recommended order for evidence submission when customers request both CAIQ/SIG and ISO artifacts? We want to avoid duplicate asks to our audit team.
2) Are there particular controls Redwood treats as FedRAMP-critical that you suggest prioritizing in the first evidence batch? Examples would be KMS key rotation attestations, hardening benchmarks, and access-control snapshots.

We attached the questionnaire skeleton we plan to use (see SIG-questionnaire-draft.xlsx). Goal: produce a clear two-week intake window for the initial batch if feasible.

Can you confirm owners and gaps by EOD tomorrow? If it's easier, loop in whoever owns FedRAMP scope.

Appreciate it — Sam

Subject: Re: SIG + CAIQ intake and ISO/FedRAMP phasing questions

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire draft. Short answers up front, with detail below: 

- Recommended submission order: CAIQ/SIG inventory first (controls + narratives), then ISO artifacts that map to the same controls (policies, evidence windows, snapshots). This reduces duplicate ticketing for your engineers.
- FedRAMP-critical controls to prioritize: KMS/crypto, change control + CI/CD provenance, privileged access reviews, logging/retention for admin APIs, and network perimeter segmentation.

Details / proposed intake plan (two-week cadence):
Week 0 (intake): HelixBank submits CAIQ/SIG spreadsheet + initial control owner list; Redwood confirms control mapping and highlights FedRAMP-critical subset.
Week 1 (core evidence): Provide KMS rotation logs, IAM access review snapshots, one week of admin API audit logs, and build pipeline SBOM/provenance.
Week 2 (supplemental): Hardening checklists, user access deprovisioning steps, encryption config exports, and expected policy docs (ISO scope/policy references).

Owners (proposed):
- Priya Natarajan — evidence routing + CAIQ mapping (I'll have her own the spreadsheet mapping).
- Kimberly Park — audit liaison for ISO/FedRAMP artefact extraction and sampling windows.

Open clarifying questions:
1) Sam, for FedRAMP do you need full historical rotation records or just the/latest rotation proof and policy? That affects how far back we pull KMS snapshots.
2) Are you accepting isolated artifacts (zips per control) or do you prefer a consolidated evidence bundle per control family?

I'll start the control map once you confirm the acceptance format. Priya / Kimberly — can you confirm your availability for a 30-min sync Friday 4/16?

Thanks,
Tessa

--

Hi all — quick note following Tessa's plan. I'm happy to own the mapping and will attach an initial evidence-index (CSV) once I complete the first pass this afternoon. A few implementation details we should lock down now so HelixBank's intake work is not re-worked: 

- Evidence format: we prefer a consolidated bundle per control family (easier for auditors), but will also provide zips per control on request. We'll include a manifest that points to the canonical snapshot for each artifact (screenshot, log excerpt, signed attestation).
- KMS rotation: for FedRAMP intake, auditors typically ask for rotation proof covering the previous 6 months plus the latest key policy. If storage cost or access is a concern on your side, we can provide sampled rotation records + key policy and then expand if requested.
- Time windows: provide the earliest acceptable snapshot timestamp for each artifact (e.g., admin API logs: 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07). That will let us pre-run extractions.

I'll upload the e2e mapping CSV as "evidence-index-2026Q2.csv" to the Drive link Tessa shared and update the CAIQ with the control IDs we reference.

Kimberly — can you confirm whether the ISO scope document we maintain internally (ISO-Scope-v2) is sufficient for HelixBank, or should we generate a tailored scope statement for them?

Thanks,
Priya
